newsitem.title: USA: JTS sees Q2 revenue shortfall.
newsitem.headline: JTS sees Q2 revenue shortfall.

text.p: JTS Corp, a maker of computer hard disk drives for desktop and notebook personal computers, said Monday it expects revenues for its second quarter ending August 2 to fall below the previous quarter's $73.4 million.

In a statement, the company said industry-wide weakness in demand for disk drives will lead to the lower revenues. It cited weak consumer demand for PCs, a disappointing market for upgrades, below-forecast sales in Europe, and a slow portable computer market.
JTS did not say how the revenue shortfall would affect second quarter earnings.
Analysts expect the company to report a loss of $0.06 a share in the quarter, according to First Call.
In the first quarter the company reported a net loss of $11.8 million, or $0.11 per share.
JTS said June shipments fell short of expectations, leading it to cut production levels. It forecast second quarter shipments below the first quarter's 540,000 disk drives.

"As we strategically focus on building a stronger business based on a higher concentration of (original equipment manufacturer) customers, it is likely that our future growth will initially be lower than historical levels," said Tom Mitchell, chief executive officer.
He said second quarter gross margin will be below 4.4 percent but added the company has taken steps to cut operatings costs.
JTS plans to announce second quarter earnings in late August.
